blocks.content: The independence of the judiciary is a basic feature of the Constitution which cannot be abrogated even by a constitutional amendment.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Judges of the Supreme Court and High Courts are guaranteed security of tenure and can only be removed by the President on grounds of proved misbehaviour or incapacity.
Salaries, allowances, and pensions of Supreme Court judges are charged directly on the Consolidated Fund of India and are non-votable by Parliament.
Article 50 under the Directive Principles of State Policy obligates the State to separate the judiciary from the executive in the public services.
The conduct of judges in the discharge of their duties cannot be discussed in Parliament or State Legislatures, except during a formal removal motion.
Retired Supreme Court judges are completely barred from pleading or acting in any court or before any authority within the territory of India.

rows: Barred from all courts and authorities in India
Allowed only in SC and High Courts other than where served

items: Pensions of High Court judges are charged on the Consolidated Fund of India, whereas their salaries and allowances are charged on the Consolidated Fund of the State.
Salaries and service conditions of judges cannot be varied to their disadvantage after appointment, except during a Financial Emergency under Article 360.
Under Article 121 and Article 211, no discussion shall take place in Parliament or State Assemblies with respect to the conduct of any judge in the discharge of duties.
